en.title: Netflix's D&D Series Dives Deep into Gothic Horror with Ravenloft
en.summary: The much-anticipated Netflix Dungeons & Dragons series is shifting gears from its initial concept to embrace the chilling atmosphere of Ravenloft. This new direction brings a gothic horror sensibility to the popular fantasy world.
en.body:
Forget The Forgotten Realms; Netflix is charting a new course for its Dungeons & Dragons television universe, and it’s a journey into the mist-shrouded Domains of Dread. While the previously announced series based on the expansive Forgotten Realms setting is no longer in development, the streamer has officially greenlit a new project focused on the iconic **Ravenloft** setting. This gothic horror campaign world, known for its brooding atmosphere and tragic villains, is set to be brought to life by a truly remarkable creative team.

Spearheading this new venture are writer and executive producer **John August**, a celebrated screenwriter known for his work on fantastical films like *Big Fish* and Disney's live-action *Aladdin*, and executive producer **Alfonso Cuarón**, the visionary director behind critically acclaimed films such as *Children of Men* and *Roma*. Together, their combined talents promise a prestige fantasy series that blends thrilling adventure with the chilling embrace of gothic horror and compelling, often tragic, romance. Hasbro Entertainment is also involved in bringing this dark corner of D&D to the screen.

## A Descent into the Domains of Dread

The **Ravenloft** setting is a departure from the high-fantasy epics often associated with Dungeons & Dragons. Instead, it plunges players and viewers into a collection of demi-planes, each ruled by a powerful and tormented Darklord. These domains are trapped within the Mists, unable to escape their cursed realities. The series is described as a "prestige fantasy series where adventure collides with gothic horror and tragic romance," focusing on character-driven stories steeped in dark magic and supernatural intrigue. At its core, the narrative will explore the creation of the legendary vampire Darklord, **Strahd von Zarovich**, delving into his tale of ambition, obsession, and lost love.

## What This Means for D&D Fans

This shift to **Ravenloft** is a significant indicator of Netflix's evolving approach to adapting Dungeons & Dragons. Moving away from a more traditional fantasy setting towards a genre known for its psychological depth and exploration of morality, the streamer is tapping into a rich vein of storytelling. Fans have long clamored for more D&D content that embraces the genre's diverse tones, and **Ravenloft** offers a perfect opportunity to explore darker themes and complex characters. The involvement of **John August** and **Alfonso Cuarón** lends significant weight to the project, suggesting a sophisticated and artistically driven adaptation that respects the source material's horror elements while offering a fresh perspective.

## What's Next

While details regarding a release date or casting have not yet been announced, the development of **Ravenloft** at Netflix signifies a promising future for Dungeons & Dragons on screen. Fans can anticipate a series that promises to be as intellectually stimulating as it is terrifying, drawing from the deep lore of **Ravenloft**'s Domains of Dread.

By Molly Templeton | Published on September 4, 2026 Screenshot: Paramount Pictures Comment 0 Share New Share Ravenloft &url= target=”_blank” title=”Twitter”> Ravenloft ” target=”_blank” title=”Pinterest”> Screenshot: Paramount Pictures If you’ve been waiting for more news on The Forgotten Realms , the Netflix D&D series announced last year, I’m sorry to say the news isn’t good: According to Deadline , that series is no longer in development. But wait! Come back! That doesn’t mean Netflix has gotten out of the D&D game. Deadline also has word that the latest D&D project in development at the streamer is Ravenloft , which will come from the extremely intriguing team of writer and executive producer John August and executive producer Alfonso Cuarón. (Hasbro Entertainment is, of course, also involved.) August is a writer who has frequently collaborated with Tim Burton; he wrote the director’s Big Fish and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory , and co-wrote Corpse Bride, Frankenweenie , and Dark Shadows . (He also co-wrote Guy Ritchie’s Aladdin .) Cuarón, of course, made the still-criminally-underappreciated Children of Men , as well as Gravity and Roma . According to Deadline, Ravenloft is “a prestige fantasy series where adventure collides with gothic horror and tragic romance.” The description continues: “Ravenloft and its Domains of Dread tackle adventure through character-driven stories of dark magic and supernatural intrigue. At its heart, the series follows the making of the vampire Darklord Strahd von Zarovich, whose story of power, love, obsession, and undead transformation charts his origins from tragic antihero to one of Dungeons & Dragons’ most notorious villains.” The Ravenloft setting was created by novelists and gamers Tracy and Laura Hickman, and I highly recommend reading the Wikipedia page about it, where you will come across such truly delightful sentences as, “The story of how Count von Zarovich became Darklord of Barovia was detailed in the 1993 novel I, Strahd: The Memoirs of a Vampire. ” (Said novel, by P.N. Elrod, sounds extremely fun.) As Deadline notes, the setting is extremely popular, and has “spawned more than a hundred official novels, tabletop RPG modules, video games, and companion rulebooks, along with countless fan creations.” As Deadline also notes, Ravenloft and the vampire Strahd were referenced in the series finale of Stranger Things . Netflix is nothing if not synergistic. Several D&D series have been announced over the last few years, and none have made it to our screens. Fingers crossed that the Darklord meets a better fate—but in the meantime, at least we still have Honor Among Thieves (pictured above). [ ed note: WE WILL ALWAYS HAVE JARNATHAN.
